newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks retreat from highs to end steady.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks retreat from highs to end steady.

text.p: SPI futures 2613 +11 US 30yr cl 6.52 -0.02
10yrbond futs 93.400 +0.015 Gold NY cl 321.35 Asia 321.95
*Stocks make way to cautious close after early surge. Trade modest, focus on individual results. Volume 266.28 million, value A$607.26 million, 1,083 stocks traded, 276 steady, 485 up, 322 down.

The Australian share market trod a wary path to a slightly firmer finish on Tuesday with one eye on Wall Street and a U.S. Federal Reserve meeting and the other on local corporate June 30 report cards.
The All Ordinaries index crept up 2.4 points to 2,620.9, while September share price index futures were 11 points higher at 2,613, a 7.9 point discount to the underlying market.

The market rebounded early as U.S. markets staged a comeback from Friday's sharp fall, but the weight of weaker metals prices hindered progress among the major miners which eventually dragged the benchmark index off its highs to the narrow finish.
"It's been a pretty average day," said one Sydney broker, noting the modest level of business and investor interest.
"There is no local news that has generated much interest -- it is all on the results at the moment."
Caution ahead of U.S. moves tonight came to the fore in the afternoon session with traders wary rather than fearful of another dramatic move.
"The U.S. Fed is meeting tonight and that will give us some more insight," said Hartley Poynton broker Justin Hondris.
"No-one is predicting any interest rate change there but if there is it will have an effect on us."
It was one of the busiest days of the profit season so far with myriad corporates announcing June 30 results.

The 22 percent Brierley Investments-owned newspaper publisher John Fairfax was the major result for the day, its shares ending a cent lower at A$3.18 after posting a 15 percent lower year net profit of A$73.94 million.
Shares in serum maker CSL Ltd jumped 32 cents to A$8.10 after a 21 percent higher year net profit of A$35.15 million, a number which impressed many traders.
"It was another good result from CSL. They seem to go from strength to strength," said the Sydney broker.
Capral Aluminium shares added three cents to A$4.48 despite a slightly lower half-year net profit of A$17.8 million.

Bendigo Bank shares ended down 19 at A$4.31 after a 13 percent lower year net profit of A$11.04 million, while fund manager Perpetual Trustees added five cents to A$9.75 after its year net profit leapt 48 percent to A$21.51 million.
Building materials and office supplies group Kalamazoo posted a nine percent higher year net profit of A$12.83 milion and saw its shares lose two cents to A$2.95.
Among the leaders Rio Tinto and WMC failed to make any ground as weaker metals prices pressured miners.

Rio Tinto shares lost 17 cents to A$20.81, while WMC shed nine cents to A$7.19. Brokers said volatile metals prices of late had hit Rio Tinto rather than talk of a renewed strike at its 70 percent owned Coal & Allied.
"Its more the metals markets. The situation had some way to go before being resolved in any case," one broker said.
Among industrials, media giant News Corp had a choppy day's trade to finish just three cents higher at A$5.95 ahead of its annual results, due Wednesday Sydney time.
Elsewhere, medical technology group Polartechnics hit new highs of A$5.00 before easing to close up 40 at A$4.90.
Brokers said the stock was still riding high on various reports recommending it as a buy following its alliance with a Ethicon, a unit of U.S.-based giant Johnson & Johnson.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to two, while about 25 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bond yields ended higher reflecting weakness in U.S. Treasuries in Asian trading and after the RBA August bulletin ran on similar lines to Governor Ian Macfarlane's speech last week.
By 5.25 p.m. (0725 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.71 percent, up on Monday's 6.67 percent.

The Australian dollar survived a scare on Tuesday when a news report suggested the Reserve Bank had said interest rates would be cut again, but it was still looking heavy and the bias was for further losses. At 5.25 p.m. (0725 GMT), the dollar stood at US$0.7360/70, down on an early US$0.7381/86 and a Monday close of US$0.7423/28.
